newsitem.title: USA: Viacom shares off after Blockbuster report. [CORRECTED 21:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Viacom shares off after Blockbuster report. [CORRECTED 21:45 GMT]

text.p: Shares of Viacom Inc fell after a newspaper reported the entertainment company might take a huge writedown on its Blockbuster Entertainment unit.
"It's a reaction to the story about Blockbuster," said George Rodriguez, senior vice president of equities at Guzman & Co. "That's probably what's causing it."
The Wednesday (corrects day from Thursday) edition of the Hollywood Reporter said Viacom might write down as much as $1 billion of Blockbuster assets.
A Viacom spokesman said the company would not comment on the report.
Viacom shares were off 15/16 at 29-5/16 Thursday afternoon.
Mario Gabelli, whose Gamco Investors and Gabelli mutual funds own a big stake in Viacom, said the stock was under pressure because of Blockbuster.
"Blockbuster is the Achilles' heel," he said. "All sorts of problems center around Blockbuster."
"Give me a long list of what can go wrong, and you can see it there," Gabelli said, including the use of cash flow and retail-related problems.
Gabelli said he would be unconcerned if Viacom took the writeoff, "It's a pencil writeoff," he said.
